subject: Urgent: Horizon Bank production latency + reserved throughput gap
messages:
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@horizonbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@horizonbank.com
Date: 2028-11-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Emerging latency and 5xx error spike on our dedicated pool (production)

Jordan —

We started seeing elevated latencies and a steady stream of 5xxs on our Redwood Dedicated pool starting ~08:30 PT this morning. Impact: customer-facing transaction enrichment calls (auth path) are experiencing timeouts and retries; our ops dashboard shows a sustained 150% increase in p95 latency and a 4.1% 5xx rate. This is directly affecting walk-up transactions for ~3% of requests during peak window.

We opened a PagerDuty incident (PD-8213) and attached a short timeline to the incident. We need an immediate mitigation plan and an estimated ETA for a durable remediation. From our side:
- We have reserved capacity under contract (DEAL-4879) — this seems like reserved throughput shortfall rather than transient noise.
- Please confirm if Redwood can authorize burst capacity for the next 2 hours or failover to a compatible hosted model while you triage.
- We will need an exec-level contact if this is going to exceed 4 hours; our CTO is on standby.

Attached: small telemetry dump and a snippet of customer error logs.

Elena Soto
VP, Platform Engineering
Horizon Bank

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@horizonbank.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com, david.kim@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2028-11-05T09:29:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Emerging latency and 5xx error spike on our dedicated pool (production)

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the PagerDuty link. We see the same signal in our monitoring. I pulled the initial metric slice and there are two visible things: sustained KV-cache backlog on the hot slot and a small kernel degradation on the 80-token path that raised CPU contention across the pool.

Immediate actions we’re initiating now (ETA within 20–30m):
- Authorization request for burst: pinging infra to open a +25% headroom burst on the affected reserved pool for 2 hours.
- Canary fallback: will open a routed fallback to a compatible quantized variant in the eu-hosted zone (no data leaves your VPC, routing stays within contract limits) for non-sensitive routes.
- Traffic shaping: ask your ops team to throttle non-critical enrichment calls if possible (we can provide a short filter).

I’ve looped in @Marissa (Customer Success) and @Rishi (SRE/Serving) to coordinate on a fast remediation and exec notification if the burst is not enough.

Will update in the next 15–30 minutes with a status and any action items.

—Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com
(415) 555-0132

Subject: Internal: Horizon Bank — rapid triage + exec escalation path (PD-8213)

Team —

Summary: Horizon Bank (DEAL-4879) is experiencing a dedicated pool saturation event resulting in elevated p95 latency (~150% above baseline) and a 5xx rate (~4%). Customer ops reports direct impact to transaction enrichment. PagerDuty incident PD-8213 is open.

Asks (urgent):
1) Rishi — please confirm root cause triage (KV cache backlog vs kernel regression) and provide an ETA to relieve contention. If we need a hot rollback or kernel revert, call it now.
2) David — can you approve a 2-hour burst headroom (+25%) for this reserved pool? If procurement/sign-off is required, mark this as exec-urgent and I will route.
3) Marissa/Kim — coordinate comms with Horizon. They’ve asked for an exec contact if this exceeds 4 hours. Prepare a short customer statement (2–3 bullets) and a credit path (SC-ops / billing).

Immediate mitigations in flight (status):
- Burst authorization requested (pending David) — ETA 10–20m if approved.
- Traffic shaping rules drafted; I’ve sent the filter to Elena’s ops for quick apply.
- Canary fallback plan to quantized-hosted variant ready to enable for non-PII routes (needs approval).

Attachments: horizon_telemetry_snapshot.csv (first 10k rows), timeline_screenshot.png, customer-ops-log.txt — dropping these to the incident and the shared drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/horizon-telemetry

If burst is denied or ineffective, escalate to execs (VP Eng / CTO) and consider automatic credit + extended remediation SLAs.

Thanks — will keep everyone updated.

—Jordan
From: Elena Soto <elena.soto@horizonbank.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@horizonbank.com, cto@horizonbank.com
Date: 2028-11-05T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Emerging latency and 5xx error spike on our dedicated pool (production)

Jordan / team —

Thanks for the quick updates and the burst authorization (we saw partial relief after the headroom increase). We still have intermittent 5xxs during the late-morning peak and are tracking a ~40% reduced error rate vs the initial window, so the mitigation helped but did not fully resolve root cause.

Next: our CTO would like a brief (15m) call with your exec on the escalation path and a written timeline for root-cause remediation + an SLA credit estimate for today’s window. Please propose times — we are available in the next 2 hours.

Also attaching a short customer impact summary from our ops team (customer-ops-log.txt).

Elena
VP, Platform Engineering
Horizon Bank
